subject: Co-sell credit conversion + onboarding fee treatment for marketplace listings
messages:
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>
To: Sarah Lim <sarah.lim@amazon.com>; AWS Partner Programs <aws-partner-programs@amazon.com>
Cc: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 25 Jun 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Co-sell credit conversion + onboarding fee treatment for marketplace listings

Hi Sarah / Partner Program team,

Quick question as we finalize the upcoming renewal: we have an outstanding item in the draft SOW related to a one-time onboarding/service fee ("Marketplace Onboarding Service") that the listing team wants to treat as a co-sell credit rather than a vendor fee so it doesn't hit Redwood's professional services budget. The asks: 1) Is there an accepted mechanism on AWS to convert one-time listing/onboarding fees into partner/co-sell credits for partner revenue recognition and incentive purposes? 2) If not standard, what paperwork or CP flow would you need (SOW addendum, joint credit memo, partner ops ticket)? 3) Any timing constraints for this to be applied against Q3 incentives?

Attached: AWS_SKU_mapping.xlsx (mapping of our offer SKUs to proposed credit buckets).

Reason for ask: if onboarding can be treated as co-sell credit, we can preserve marketing & PS budgets and keep marketplace economics cleaner for renewals. Vanessa / Karthik — looping you in for any finance or legal constraints.

Thanks,
Hannah
Hannah Schmitt
Head of Cloud Partnerships (Marketplace Programs)
Redwood Inference

From: Sarah Lim <sarah.lim@amazon.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>
Cc: AWS Partner Programs <aws-partner-programs@amazon.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 25 Jun 2027 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Co-sell credit conversion + onboarding fee treatment for marketplace listings

Hi Hannah — thanks for the clear write-up and the SKU mapping. Short answer: AWS does have pathways to treat certain onboarding/enablement spend as eligible for partner credit, but it depends on how the activity is invoiced and whether it maps to approved co-sell/enablement line items.

High level we need:
- A one-page summary tying the onboarding deliverables to eligible co-sell activities (joint enablement, customer workshops, technical enablement).
- An internal Partner Ops request (I can raise this but will need your SOW addendum and an itemized invoice).
- Confirmation from your finance team that Redwood will recognize this as a credit and not a reimbursable PS invoice (helps our audit).

Timing: if you want it to hit Q3 credits we need the Partner Ops request and supporting docs by July 9. I can expedite once we have the SOW addendum.

I'll also loop Carlos from GCP in case you plan a similar conversion there — rules differ but the paperwork ask is similar.

Cheers,
Sarah
Sarah Lim
AWS Partner Programs
[Attachment: partner-credit-guidelines.pdf]

From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Sarah Lim <sarah.lim@amazon.com>
Date: Fri, 25 Jun 2027 13:42:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Co-sell credit conversion + onboarding fee treatment for marketplace listings

Thanks Sarah — good to know there is a path. Two quick finance/legal notes from our side: 

1) Contract alignment: Legal needs the SOW addendum language to explicitly state the fee is "dedicated to joint enablement activities and eligible for partner credit" — otherwise it will default to our services revenue line.
2) Revenue recognition: Finance prefers we treat the amount as a contra-revenue credit (to be netted against marketplace revenue) rather than a reduction in PS revenue. If AWS requires an invoice, we need to ensure it is labeled "Enablement/Co-sell Credit Eligible" and accompanied by the one-page deliverable summary.

I've drafted a short addendum template and attached a term sheet with the proposed credit mapping — see proposed_co_sell_credit_term_sheet.pdf. If legal signs off on the wording I can send the Partner Ops request to Sarah on Monday.

Vanessa Ortiz
Director, Finance — Partnerships
Redwood Inference
[Attachment: proposed_co_sell_credit_term_sheet.pdf]

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Sarah Lim <sarah.lim@amazon.com>, Carlos Mendez <carlos.m@partnerops.gcp.com>
Date: Fri, 25 Jun 2027 16:38:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Co-sell credit conversion + onboarding fee treatment for marketplace listings

All — decision summary and next steps: 

- We will proceed with treating the onboarding fee as co-sell credit eligible pending: legal-approved SOW addendum + itemized invoice + one-page deliverables summary.
- Vanessa to finalize the addendum language by Monday (6/28).
- Hannah to provide the itemized deliverable list and final SKU mapping (confirm last column in AWS_SKU_mapping.xlsx) by EOD 6/29.
- Hannah/Vanessa: once docs are ready I authorize Sarah to raise Partner Ops on our behalf to try and capture Q3 credit (Sarah: flagged deadline July 9).

If GCP requires different paperwork, Carlos please advise; otherwise we will replicate the same packet for GCP.

Thanks — Karthik
Karthik Iyer
VP, Business Ops & GTM Strategy
Redwood Inference
